story: Rainmaker Technology Corporation seeded clouds over the Kenai Peninsula and published a rainfall figure that is a modeled counterfactual, bracketed by its own report by more than a factor of two

claims.claim: Rainmaker Technology Corporation says it conducted drone based glaciogenic cloud seeding in the Kenai Peninsula on August 23rd, 2026.
claims.verbatim: Rainmaker has successfully validated the impact of drone-based, glaciogenic cloud seeding operations in the Kenai Peninsula, AK on August 23, 2026.
claims.notes: Both company posts of August 24th give August 23rd only. August 22nd appears nowhere in either company document.

claims.claim: Rainmaker reports it executed seven coordinated seeding missions over a three hour period.
claims.verbatim: Over a three-hour period, it executed seven coordinated seeding missions, responding to a strengthening low pressure system spinning in the Gulf of Alaska that brought northeasterly flow.
claims.notes: The company's companion summary post published the same day says 10 seeding flights. See C18. The company does not reconcile them.

claims.claim: Rainmaker reports that 19 red silver iodide flares were released during the operation.
claims.verbatim: Across the seven coordinated seeding missions, 19 red flares were released by drones EL-151 and EL-153 between 06:38:18 and 09:33:41 UTC (Table 1).
claims.notes: Corroborated independently by Alaska Watchman, which reported the same count of 19 flares.

claims.claim: Rainmaker names two drones in the operation, identified as EL-151 and EL-153.
claims.verbatim: 19 red flares were released by drones EL-151 and EL-153 between 06:38:18 and 09:33:41 UTC
claims.notes: The report states missions 4 through 7 were flown solely by EL-151, two flares per mission.

claims.claim: Rainmaker reports the flares dispersed approximately 374.3 grams of silver iodide in total.
claims.verbatim: Each flare dispersed approximately 19.7 g of AgI over a nominal 3.5-min seeding period, for a total of approximately 374.3 g of AgI.
claims.notes: 19 flares times 19.7 g equals 374.3 g. Internally consistent.

claims.claim: Rainmaker reports the flare releases occurred between 06:38:18 and 09:33:41 UTC.
claims.verbatim: 19 red flares were released by drones EL-151 and EL-153 between 06:38:18 and 09:33:41 UTC
claims.notes: Alaska Daylight Time is UTC minus 8, so this ran overnight local.

claims.claim: Rainmaker reports all median release temperatures fell within the approximate minus 5 to minus 15 degrees Celsius silver iodide activation window.
claims.verbatim: Thermodynamic conditions at release altitude were favorable for AgI activation throughout the sequence, with all median release temperatures falling within the approximate -5 to -15°C activation window.
claims.notes: The physical precondition for glaciogenic seeding to work at all.

claims.claim: Rainmaker reports soundings launched from the seeding site placed the average freezing level near 1,874 metres above mean sea level.
claims.verbatim: Soundings launched from the seeding site placed the average freezing level near 1,874 m MSL.
claims.notes: Soundings are a genuine in situ measurement, unlike the precipitation figure. Useful contrast.

claims.claim: Rainmaker reports the wet area attributed to seeding covered 249.53 square kilometres, defined as accumulated seeded precipitation exceeding 0.01 millimetres.
claims.verbatim: The resulting wet area, defined by accumulated seeded precipitation exceeding 0.01 mm, covered 249.53 km².
claims.notes: The area is defined by a modelled threshold of a hundredth of a millimetre, not by anyone standing in it. About 96.3 square miles.

claims.claim: Rainmaker states the WSR-88D radar at PAHG provides the principal observational basis for the analysis.
claims.verbatim: The WSR-88D (PAHG NEXRAD) provides the principal observational basis for this analysis.
claims.notes: PAHG is the National Weather Service NEXRAD at Middleton Island. The instrument is public and federal, the inference is the company's.

claims.claim: Rainmaker estimated the natural background by subtracting 5 dBZ from all radar gates before converting reflectivity to precipitation.
claims.verbatim: 5 dBZ was subtracted from all radar gates prior to conversion to liquid-equivalent precipitation using the Z–S relationship.
claims.notes: The counterfactual step and the load bearing assumption of the whole figure. The rain that would have fallen anyway is not observed, it is assumed to be the observed signal minus a flat offset.

claims.claim: Rainmaker converted radar reflectivity to precipitation using 27 separate relationships of the form Z equals a times S to the power b.
claims.verbatim: Reflectivity is converted to liquid-equivalent snowfall rate using 27 relationships of the form Z = aS^b.
claims.notes: The 27 relationships are what generate the spread in the final range. The ensemble is the source of the uncertainty band, a point in the company's favour on transparency.

claims.claim: Rainmaker uses the verb estimates for the net new precipitation figure.
claims.value: 45 to 65 acre feet, mean 57.6 acre feet
claims.verbatim: Rainmaker estimates these seeding signatures created 45
claims.notes: The central claim of the deck. The company itself writes estimates. The full source sentence carries an em dash between 45 and 65, so the verbatim is truncated before it rather than reproducing a banned mark. 57.6 acre feet is about 18.8 million US gallons at 325,851 gallons per acre foot.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's own report gives a 5th to 95th percentile range of 41.70 to 89.35 acre feet around a mean of 57.62 acre feet.
claims.verbatim: the mean precipitation volume attributed to seeding was 57.62 acre-feet (71,072 m³), with a 5th–95th percentile range of 41.70–89.35 acre-feet.
claims.notes: The single most important number for this deck. The upper bound is 2.14 times the lower bound. In gallons at 325,851 per acre foot that is roughly 13.6 million to 29.1 million, against a headline of 19 million. The gallon conversion is the studio's arithmetic from two cited figures.

claims.claim: Rainmaker states its uncertainty range does not account for what happens to precipitation between the lowest radar beam and the ground.
claims.verbatim: Importantly, this range does not account for uncertainty associated with the evolution of precipitation between the lowest radar beam (~1800–2200 m MSL) and the surface.
claims.notes: The company's own caveat. The radar sees roughly two kilometres up and the claim is about water reaching the ground, so the published band is a floor on the uncertainty rather than a ceiling. Credit the company for disclosing it.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's summary post states the operation generated approximately 19 million gallons of water in a three hour period.
claims.verbatim: That's approximately 19 million gallons of water generated in a three hour period.
claims.notes: Key structural finding. The gallons figure lives in the summary post, not in the technical validation report, which works in acre feet throughout. The headline number and the uncertainty band were published the same day in two different documents.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's summary post gives the figure as a mean of 57 acre feet with an interquartile range of 45 to 65 acre feet.
claims.verbatim: Rainmaker generated a mean of 57 acre-feet of rain (IQR: 45
claims.notes: The summary post quotes the interquartile range, which is narrower than the 5th to 95th range in the technical report. Both are the company's own numbers, and the wider band is in the less read document. Verbatim truncated before the source's em dash.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's summary post says the company made 10 seeding flights on August 23rd between 6:30am and 9:23am UTC.
claims.verbatim: On August 23, Rainmaker made 10 seeding flights between 6:30am and 9:23am UTC, igniting AgI flares into clouds between 3,500 and 4,200 meters MSL.
claims.notes: Same day, same company, seven missions in one document and 10 flights in the other. Do not assert an error, state both and note the company does not reconcile them.

claims.claim: Rainmaker says it has operated in the Kenai Peninsula since June 2026.
claims.verbatim: Rainmaker has operated in the Kenai Peninsula, Alaska since June.
claims.notes: The August 23rd operation was not a one off visit. Year inferred from the post's own August 2026 date.

claims.claim: Rainmaker says it chose the region for a high incidence of summertime seeding conditions along the Chugach and Kenai coastal ranges.
claims.verbatim: The region was chosen for a high incidence of summertime seeding conditions along the Chugach and Kenai coastal ranges, enabling Rainmaker to conduct flight testing and validation research.
claims.notes: The company's stated reason is research and flight testing conditions. No client, contract or water customer is named anywhere in either post.

claims.claim: Rainmaker says it followed methodology established by the National Center for Atmospheric Research in the 2017 SNOWIE campaign.
claims.verbatim: Using methodology established by the National Center for Atmospheric Research in the 2017 SNOWIE campaign
claims.notes: SNOWIE is a real published campaign and the technical report separately cites Friedrich et al. 2020. The paper itself was not fetched, so this is the company's own claim of lineage.

claims.claim: Rainmaker describes Stratus as a proprietary forecasting and nowcasting platform that ingests realtime weather data to identify optimal seeding windows.
claims.verbatim: Rainmaker's proprietary forecasting and nowcasting platform ingests realtime weather data to identify optimal seeding windows and inform site planning & operational deployment.
claims.notes: Important limit. The page names no machine learning algorithm or method behind Stratus. Say the software picks when and where to fly, never that it makes rain. Undated company page, fetched on the run date.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's technology page advertises 20 plus data integrations and 5 day advanced awareness of seeding conditions.
claims.verbatim: 5-day advanced awareness of seeding conditions
claims.notes: Marketing copy on the company's own product page, not a validated performance figure. Attribute as a company claim.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's technology page claims 8,000 plus telemetry data variables in its validation stack.
claims.verbatim: 8k+ telemetry data variables
claims.notes: Company marketing figure with no method behind it. Use only with attribution.

claims.claim: Atmo and Rainmaker announced a strategic alliance for AI powered precision cloud seeding on July 14th, 2025.
claims.verbatim: Rainmaker and Atmo Announce Strategic Alliance to Transform Weather Modification with AI-Powered Precision Cloud Seeding
claims.notes: Background, outside the run window, label it as such. It is the primary source for the deep learning targeting layer.

claims.claim: Atmo claims its ensemble deep learning models predict weather up to 40,000 times faster and up to 100 times more precisely than conventional weather models.
claims.verbatim: Atmo's ensemble deep learning models, which predict weather up to 40,000 times faster and up to 100x more precisely than conventional weather models
claims.notes: Vendor claim in a joint press release with no benchmark cited. Must be hedged. Do not state as fact.

claims.claim: The Rainmaker and Atmo announcement puts drone seeding operating cost at approximately 50 dollars per flight hour including materials.
claims.verbatim: approximately $50 per flight hour including materials
claims.notes: Company stated cost, not audited. It is the economic reason drones displaced crewed aircraft here.

claims.claim: Rainmaker chief executive Augustus Doricko said the company can combine AI meteorology with radar validated cloud seeding to deliver measurable precipitation enhancement.
claims.verbatim: For the first time, we can combine AI meteorology with radar-validated cloud seeding operations to deliver measurable precipitation enhancement with extreme accuracy and cost-effectiveness.
claims.notes: Note the word measurable in the chief executive's own framing, against the word estimates in the report thirteen months later. That contrast is the deck's spine and it is fair because both strings are verbatim.

claims.claim: Rainmaker Technology Corporation is based in El Segundo, California.
claims.verbatim: Based in El Segundo, California
claims.notes: Undated company page, fetched on the run date.

claims.claim: The Federal Register published a summary of Rainmaker Technology Corporation's petition for exemption from 14 CFR 107.36 on July 29th, 2025 under docket FAA-2025-1630.
claims.verbatim: Petition for Exemption; Summary of Petition Received; Rainmaker Technology Corporation
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration via the Federal Register
claims.notes: Document number 2025-14285. Comments closed August 18th, 2025. Regulations.gov record FAA-2025-1630-0004 with 3 comments as of the Federal Register's last check on August 20th, 2025.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's FAA petition seeks authorization to use burn in place and ejectable flares on its Elijah quadcopter drones for precipitation enhancement.
claims.verbatim: Rainmaker Elijah Quadcopter Series small UAS
claims.source_outlet: Federal Aviation Administration via the Federal Register
claims.notes: Section 107.36 is the small unmanned aircraft rule prohibiting carriage of hazardous material. The drone series name matches the EL prefix on the Alaska drone identifiers in C04.

claims.claim: As of August 27th, 2026 the Federal Register contains no grant or denial of Rainmaker's exemption petition, only the July 2025 notice of the petition.
claims.verbatim: Petition for Exemption; Summary of Petition Received; Rainmaker Technology Corporation
claims.notes: Verified absence. A docket_id query on the Federal Register API returned exactly one document, the petition notice. The FAA posts many exemption decisions to regulations.gov without a Federal Register notice, and regulations.gov returned 403 to every fetch, so this proves no Federal Register decision rather than no decision at all. Phrase it as no decision has been published in the Federal Register.

claims.claim: NOAA requires anyone conducting weather modification in the United States to report it at least 10 days before undertaking the activity.
claims.verbatim: required by the Weather Modification Act of 1976
claims.notes: The page states companies must report to the Administrator of NOAA at least 10 days prior to undertaking the activity. Forms are NOAA 17-4 initial and 17-4A interim and final, filed to weather.modification@noaa.gov, and failure to report can bring fines of up to 10,000 dollars. Two fetches returned different citation strings, so cite the requirement rather than a section number.

claims.claim: NOAA's public list of weather modification project reports could not be read to confirm or refute a Rainmaker filing for the Alaska operation.
claims.verbatim: Last Updated: Feb 27, 2026 10:12 AM
claims.notes: Honest negative. The project list is a JavaScript datatable that did not render, and the page's own stamp predates the operation by six months. This is a gap in the record, not evidence that no filing was made.

claims.claim: No chapter of Alaska Statutes Title 46, which covers water, air, energy and environmental conservation, addresses weather modification or cloud seeding.
claims.value: no weather modification chapter in Title 46
claims.verbatim: Chapter 15. Water Use Act
claims.notes: State the narrow finding only. The fetched chapter list runs Environmental Conservation through Chapter 45, including Air Quality Control and the Water Use Act, with nothing on weather modification. This is a secondary mirror, and akleg.gov, dec.alaska.gov, law.justia.com and ncsl.org all returned 403, so the state's own statute text and DEC's permit list went unchecked. Do not claim Alaska has no weather modification law anywhere in its code.

claims.claim: The Kenai Peninsula Borough has a land area of 16,017.53 square miles.
claims.notes: Land area 41,485,210,464 square metres, which is 41,485.21 square kilometres. Against C09 the 249.53 square kilometre affected area is about 0.6 percent of the borough's land area. That ratio is the studio's arithmetic from two cited figures.

claims.claim: A search of named Alaska outlets on August 27th, 2026 found only the Alaska Watchman had covered the Rainmaker Kenai Peninsula operation.
claims.verbatim: Chemically seeded clouds over Alaska results in 19-million-gallon rainfall in 3 hours
claims.notes: Outlets checked and returning nothing on this operation. Anchorage Daily News, Peninsula Clarion, Alaska Public Media, KDLL Kenai. KSRM Radio Kenai returned 403 and could not be checked. The Kenai Peninsula Borough's own site does not mention it. Say a search of named outlets found no coverage, never that none exists.

claims.claim: The Alaska Watchman headlined a single 19 million gallon figure while its own body reported the company's range.
claims.verbatim: Rainmaker then calculated that the operation produced a net increase of roughly 15
claims.notes: The body says roughly 15 to 21 million gallons, arithmetically faithful to the company's 45 to 65 acre feet band. The headline collapses it to one number, and the article never mentions the wider 41.70 to 89.35 band. The same collapse happens in the company's own summary post, so the point is not partisan. Verbatim truncated before the source's en dash.

claims.claim: Rainmaker's flare releases ran from 06:38 to 09:33 UTC on August 23rd, which is the evening of August 22nd in Alaska Daylight Time.
claims.verbatim: 19 red flares were released by drones EL-151 and EL-153 between 06:38:18 and 09:33:41 UTC
claims.notes: Alaska Daylight Time is UTC minus 8. This is the most likely innocent explanation for the Alaska Watchman dating the operation across two days while the company gives one. The date arithmetic is the studio's, from the company's own UTC stamps.

claims.claim: The Alaska Watchman reported that the Air Line Pilots Association warned Rainmaker's technology poses an extreme safety risk.
claims.verbatim: the Air Line Pilots Association has warned that the Rainmaker technology poses 'an extreme safety risk,' included airspace integration, flare debris/fire hazards, and lack of certain modeling.
claims.notes: Attribution framed on purpose. What is verified is that Alaska Watchman published this, not that ALPA said it. Regulations.gov returned 403 on the docket, the comment page and the document page, and alpa.org returned 403. The Federal Register record does confirm 3 comments were filed on docket FAA-2025-1630. If used it must read according to the Alaska Watchman, and it is safer to omit.

killed.claim: The seeding operation ran on August 22nd and 23rd, 2026.
killed.why: August 22nd appears in no company document. Both posts give August 23rd only. The two day span comes from Alaska Watchman and is most likely the UTC to Alaska Daylight Time offset, recorded at C39.

killed.claim: The validation report claims 19 million gallons of rain.
killed.why: It does not. A targeted fetch found no occurrence of gallons or 19 million in the technical report, which works in acre feet throughout. Conflating the two would be the exact error the deck is criticising.

killed.claim: The Air Line Pilots Association filed a comment objecting to Rainmaker's FAA petition on safety grounds.
killed.why: Could not be independently verified. Regulations.gov and alpa.org both returned 403. Survives only in the attribution framed form at C40.

killed.claim: Rainmaker filed the required NOAA Form 17-4 for the Alaska operation.
killed.why: Unprovable either way. NOAA's project report list is a JavaScript datatable that did not render and its last updated stamp is six months before the operation.

killed.claim: Rainmaker did not report the operation to NOAA.
killed.why: Same reason in the other direction. An unreadable list is not an empty list. Asserting a missing filing would be the single most defamatory error available here.

killed.claim: The FAA has granted or denied Rainmaker's exemption petition.
killed.why: No decision document exists in the Federal Register for docket FAA-2025-1630. Regulations.gov, where the FAA posts most exemption decisions, was unreachable, so the honest statement is that no decision has been published in the Federal Register.

killed.claim: Alaska has no weather modification statute or permit requirement.
killed.why: Too strong. Only Title 46's chapter list was confirmed, via a secondary mirror, and four state and national sources returned 403.

killed.claim: The Kenai Peninsula Borough or any Alaska state body was notified of the operation.
killed.why: No evidence in either direction. Absence of a mention is not proof of absence of notice.

killed.claim: The operation was conducted for a client, or was connected to Bradley Lake hydro or any water user.
killed.why: Nothing supports it. Both company posts describe flight testing and validation research and name no customer.

killed.claim: Nineteen million gallons of rain fell on the Kenai Peninsula in three hours.
killed.why: Category error, and the deck's whole point. The figure is a net difference between an observed radar field and a modelled background produced by subtracting a flat 5 dBZ. Nobody measured 19 million gallons.

killed.claim: It rained for three hours because of the seeding.
killed.why: The three hours is the operational window from first to last flare, not a duration of rainfall attributable to seeding.

killed.claim: The Kenai Peninsula Borough covers 25,600 square miles.
killed.why: That figure describes the borough school district service area, not the borough's land area. Census gazetteer land area is 16,017.53 square miles, used at C36.

killed.claim: Rainmaker's AI decides where and when it rains.
killed.why: Overstates the fetched sources. Stratus is described as forecasting and nowcasting that identifies seeding windows and informs site planning, and no algorithm is named. The software targets the flight. The physics after flare ignition is not claimed to be AI directed.

killed.claim: The word measured does not appear anywhere in the validation report.
killed.why: Directionally supported but too absolute to publish on a single fetch of a JavaScript rendered page. The provable version is C13.
